name: Waldorf Blofeld
description: Waldorf Blofeld synthesizer (desktop and keyboard): every sound parameter of its SysEx specification, sent to the Sound mode edit buffer, with identity and Pull from that edit buffer.

sources.title: Blofeld System Exclusive Specifications, software release 1.04
sources.notes: Sound data table, value lists, effect parameters and messages read by tools/profiles/waldorf/read-waldorf-sysex.mjs from Blofeld_sysex_v1_04.pdf (sha256 6d3b6557b2a8ee377ff517460ec920a1dd8b576506f47d2bf40c553af82c80d5), https://downloads.waldorfmusic.com/cloud/index.php/s/ybExJgT4TzqT8ir/download/Blofeld_sysex_v1_04.pdf. Not yet checked against the instrument itself.

authoringNotes: Generated by tools/profiles/waldorf/make-profiles.mjs; edit the layout in tools/profiles/waldorf/synths/, not this file.
Every parameter is a row of the specification's sound data table, with its printed name. Nothing here has been sent to a real instrument yet.

Sound parameter change: F0 3E 13 <dev> 20 00 <HH> <PP> <value> F7, HH PP the parameter's index (its offset in the sound dump) in two 7-bit bytes, to the Sound mode edit buffer. <dev> is the deviceId variable, the instrument's Device ID (0 unless set otherwise); its dumps are matched by it too.
Identity: the reply the specification prints, family 13 00, member 00 00 (Blofeld Desktop).

The Blofeld's spec prints the sound request's checksum byte in its format line and leaves it out of the table beneath; the Microwave 2's, its ancestor, prints it as (BB+NN) & 7F, which for the edit buffer (7F 00) is 7F, the value the spec says is always accepted. The request carries it.
In Multi mode the same parameter change reaches instrument 1's sound (location 00); the other instruments (01 - 0F) are not laid out.
The global parameters (GLBD) have no parameter change, and are not laid out.

Read through this profile, Waldorf's Blofeld factory sounds (2008 and 2012, 2,048 sounds) all match the sound dump and pass its checksum. A few hold values neither the spec nor the manual lists: modulation destinations 54 - 57 (29 times, in slots 9 - 16 only; both documents stop at 53, M4 Amount), oscillator octaves between the steps of 12 (e.g. 47, 102), and envelope mode bytes 64 and 47 (8 times). A Pull of such a sound shows the number. Two of the 2012 sounds have a 02 byte in their names, read as ?.
Rows the reader could not split, given by the layout: 317 Arpeggiator Direction.

Left out, a byte of bit fields whose fields have no lists to enumerate: 327 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 1, 328 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 2, 329 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 3, 330 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 4, 331 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 5, 332 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 6, 333 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 7, 334 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 8, 335 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 9, 336 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 10, 337 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 11, 338 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 12, 339 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 13, 340 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 14, 341 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 15, 342 Arp Pattern Step/Glide/Accent 16, 343 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 1, 344 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 2, 345 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 3, 346 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 4, 347 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 5, 348 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 6, 349 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 7, 350 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 8, 351 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 9, 352 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 10, 353 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 11, 354 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 12, 355 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 13, 356 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 14, 357 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 15, 358 Arp Pattern Timing/Length 16.
